Ecovyst Inc. and subsidiaries is a leading provider of regenerated sulfuric acid, virgin sulfuric acid and sulfur dioxide and related derivatives, which we believe are essential to our customers' operations and processes. Our family of virgin sulfuric acid products, regenerated sulfuric acid and related derivatives serve a wide range of industrial applications. We are a leading provider of regenerated sulfuric acid to the North American refining industry for the production of alkylate, an essential gasoline component for lowering vapor pressure and increasing octane to meet stringent gasoline specifications and fuel efficiency standards. We are a leading North American producer of high quality and high strength virgin sulfuric acid for industrial and mining applications. Through our Calabrian business, we are also a leading producer of sulfur dioxide and related derivatives in North America, serving key end uses including mining, water treatment and specialty chemical production. We also provide chemical waste handling and treatment services, as well as ex-situ catalyst activation services for the refining and petrochemical industry. For more information, see our website at https://www.ecovyst.com . title: June 2025: Preferred Drivers feature is here

Your operation runs better when the right people are behind the wheel. Start building your all-star lineup today.

title: Introducing Built-in Tools for Mastra Agents
summary: Five ready-to-use tools for common agent tasks.
body_text: Your Mastra agents can now use five built-in tools for common tasks like: creating a TODO list, or searching the web. The following tools are included in @mastra/core and can be used with both agents and workflows: Keeping a durable task list Searching the web Fetching a URL Asking users questions Submitting plans for approval Your browser does not support the video tag. If you're prototyping an agent, built-in tools can get you up and running faster, and when you’re ready, you can swap them out for provider-specific tools. All built-in tools integrate with Studio — task lists render as a live panel, ask-user prompts as a chat pause, and plan approvals as an approve/reject card, making it easier to interact and test your agent during development. Get started Install @mastra/core : Terminal npm install @mastra/core note TaskSignalProvider : added in 1.42.0 , PR #17820 . webSearchTool : added in 1.55.0 , PR #20345 . webFetchTool : added in 1.54.0 , PR #20232 . askUserTool : added in 1.42.0 , PR #17806 . submitPlanTool : added in 1.42.0 , PR #17817 . Task tracking Manage a durable, thread-scoped task list — write, update, complete, and check tasks. Available using TaskSignalProvider , which registers four task tools ( task_write , task_check , task_update , and task_complete ). Memory is required to persist list states. src/mastra/agents/task-tracking-agent.ts import { Agent } from " @mastra/core/agent " ; import { Memory } from " @mastra/memory " ; import { TaskSignalProvider } from " @mastra/core/signals " ; export const taskTrackingAgent = new Agent ({ id: " task-tracking-agent " , name: " Task Tracking Agent " , instructions: " Track your progress with the task tools. " , model: " anthropic/claude-opus-5 " , memory: new Memory (), signals: [ new TaskSignalProvider ()] }); Web search Use the model's native web search capability. Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, and xAI: src/mastra/agents/web-search-agent.ts import { Agent } from " @mastra/core/agent " ; import { webSearchTool } from " @mastra/core/tools " ; export const webSearchAgent = new Agent ({ id: " web-search-agent " , name: " Web Search Agent " , instructions: " Use web search when you need current information. " , model: " anthropic/claude-opus-5 " , tools: { webSearchTool } }); Web fetch Fetch a URL over HTTP or HTTPS and return the page's text content. Blocks localhost and private IPs, follows up to 5 redirects, and truncates at 100,000 characters: src/mastra/agents/web-fetch-agent.ts import { Agent } from " @mastra/core/agent " ; import { webFetchTool } from " @mastra/core/tools " ; export const webFetchAgent = new Agent ({ id: " web-fetch-agent " , name: " Web Fetch Agent " , instructions: " Fetch the page the user links to before answering. " , model: " anthropic/claude-opus-5 " , tools: { webFetchTool } }); Ask user Suspend the run to ask the user a question, then resume with their answer. Supports free-text, single-select, and multi-select prompts. src/mastra/agents/ask-user-agent.ts import { Agent } from " @mastra/core/agent " ; import { askUserTool } from " @mastra/core/tools " ; export const askUserAgent = new Agent ({ id: " ask-user-agent " , name: " Ask User Agent " , instructions: " Ask the user for clarification when the request is ambiguous. " , model: " anthropic/claude-opus-5 " , tools: { askUserTool } }); Submit plan Suspend the run with a plan file path so the user can approve or reject it. Pair with workspace tools so the agent can write the plan file before submitting. src/mastra/agents/submit-plan-agent.ts import { Agent } from " @mastra/core/agent " ; import { submitPlanTool } from " @mastra/core/tools " ; import { LocalFilesystem, Workspace, mkdirTool, readFileTool, writeFileTool } from " @mastra/core/workspace " ; export const submitPlanAgent = new Agent ({ id: " submit-plan-agent " , name: " Submit Plan Agent " , instructions: " You draft plans and submit them for review. " , model: " anthropic/claude-opus-5 " , workspace: new Workspace ({ id: " submit-plan-workspace " , filesystem: new LocalFilesystem ({ basePath: process. cwd () }) }), tools: { submitPlanTool, writeFileTool, readFileTool, mkdirTool } }); For more information and full configuration options, see: Built-in tools Task tools reference TaskSignalProvider reference webSearchTool webFetchTool askUserTool reference submitPlanTool reference Workspace overview

title: Andersen Group Delivers Record Second-Quarter Revenue of $217.7 Million
summary: Six-Month Revenue Reaches $458.4 Million, Up 19.4%, with All Service Lines Contributing to Broad-Based Growth SAN FRANCISCO--(BUSINESS…...
body_text: Andersen Group Delivers Record Second-Quarter Revenue of $217.7 Million August 12, 2026 4:15pm EDT Download as PDF Related Documents Earnings Webcast Audio 10-Q HTML XBRL Zip Six-Month Revenue Reaches $458.4 Million, Up 19.4%, with All Service Lines Contributing to Broad-Based Growth SAN FRANCISCO--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Andersen Group Inc. (NYSE: ANDG) today reported robust financial results for the second quarter and six months ended June 30, 2026, marked by accelerating revenue growth, expanding client demand, and a sharp rise in underlying profitability. Momentum Builds Across the Platform Andersen delivered second-quarter revenue of $217.7 million, up 23.7% from $176.0 million in the prior-year quarter — continuing a multi-year trend of double-digit growth. For the first six months of 2026, revenue reached $458.4 million, up 19.4% from $384.1 million in the same period last year. This revenue growth was fueled by strong client additions, higher volumes, and continued service line expansion — with every service line posting revenue growth in both the quarter and the six-month period, and with no reliance on one-time items to drive the results. This broad-based strength underscores the durability of Andersen's diversified platform and the growing demand for its multi-dimensional service offering, led by consistent revenue in the Tax practice and accelerating momentum in Andersen Consulting. Underlying Profitability Strength as Equity Compensation Normalizes Reported results for the quarter and six months reflect equity-based compensation expense, a non-cash item tied to Andersen's talent and retention strategy. Notably, equity-based compensation expense declined meaningfully to $48.3 million in the second quarter of 2026, down from $129.6 million in the second quarter of 2025 — and totaled $93.9 million for the six months, also well below the $129.6 million recorded in the same period last year. As a result of the timing and magnitude of this non-cash expense relative to the prior year, the Company reported a net loss of $10.1 million ($0.08 basic / $0.09 diluted per share) in the second quarter and a net loss of $96.0 million in the prior year quarter a year ago. Management views the strong and growing adjusted net income figures as the clearer signal of the business's underlying momentum, with equity-based compensation expense expected to continue moderating as a percentage of revenue. Andersen's core earnings power continued to improve, with adjusted net income rising to $39.0 million in the second quarter, up 38.8% from $28.1 million a year ago, and to $106.3 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026, up 27.5% from $83.3 million in the prior-year period. This growth reflects the operating leverage inherent in Andersen's scalable model as revenue outpaced expenses during the six months ended June 30, 2026. Looking Ahead Reaffirm Full-Year 2026 Guidance: Revenue expected to be in the range of approximately $980 million to $1 billion, equating to a growth rate of approximately 18%. Adjusted EBITDA projected in the range of approximately $225 million to $250 million with Adjusted EBITDA margins in the range of approximately 23% to 25%. Investing in Tomorrow's Growth: 2026 will reflect continued strategic investment in talent, technology, automation, and AI, as well as the integration of newly acquired firms — positioning Andersen for an anticipated return to full-year net income and positive EPS while building durable long-term capacity. A Platform Built for the Long Term: Andersen believes it remains well positioned for sustained revenue growth and expanding margins, backed by a large and growing addressable market, differentiated competitive positioning, a highly scalable operating model, and disciplined, selective M&A. Disciplined Capital Deployment: Andersen remains committed to deploying capital strategically to strengthen and expand its multi-dimensional platform, with a continued focus on driving long-term shareholder value. Mark L. Vorsatz, Global Chairman and CEO of Andersen, said: “Our results speak for themselves,” said Mark Vorsatz, Global Chairman and CEO of Andersen. “Revenue grew 23.7% in the quarter, every service line contributed, and adjusted net income grew even faster than revenue — indicating that our platform is scaling efficiently even as we invest aggressively in talent, technology, and AI. The reported net loss is simply a function of non-cash equity compensation; it doesn't reflect the momentum we're building. We like where this business is headed.” Recent Developments—Inorganic Growth Opportunities Andersen’s relationships with over 400 Andersen Global and Andersen Consulting member and collaborating firms provide opportunities for domestic and international expansion through closer partnerships, future acquisitions and future business combinations. In the second quarter of 2026, the Company closed the acquisitions of tax firms in Ireland and New Zealand, a tax firm and a consulting firm in Nigeria, and a tax firm and a law firm in Uruguay, expanding its presence across key developed and high-growth markets as it continues to scale its global platform. In addition, in the third quarter of 2026, Andersen closed the acquisition of a tax firm in Switzerland and a business combination in Canada and entered into definitive agreements for the acquisitions of a tax and legal firm in Mexico and a tax firm in the United Kingdom and six consulting firms in the United States. These eight additional acquisitions are expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to the satisfaction of certain closing conditions. We provide services in four primary areas: Private Client Services. We provide comprehensive tax and financial services for individuals and families, addressing complex client matters such as multigenerational wealth, charitable giving and trust and estate planning. Business Tax Services. Alternative Investment Funds. Non-GAAP Financial Measures Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted Net Income Margin We define Adjusted Net Income as net income plus expenses related to transaction activities, including costs related to planned mergers, acquisitions, and business combinations, non-recurring equity restructuring costs and non-cash equity-based compensation expense. We define Adjusted Net Income Margin as Adjusted Net Income divided by revenue. We believe Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted Net Income Margin enhance an investor’s understanding of our financial and operating performance because they exclude transaction-related costs allowing for greater transparency into what measures we use in operating our business and measuring our performance. In addition, these measures enable comparison of financial trends and results between periods. In the second quarter of 2026, we revised our definition of Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted Net Income Margin to include all non-cash equity-based compensation, and in the last twelve months ended June 30, 2026, non-cash equity-based compensation expense for LTIP Units and restricted stock units were added to conform to the current presentation. The change is intended to provide a more meaningful measure of our underlying operating performance by excluding equity-based compensation charges which are non-cash in nature and do not reflect our core operating results. The additional adjustments are consistent with our treatment of other equity-based compensation expenses and are intended to provide greater consistency in presentation. We applied the revised definition consistently to current and comparative periods, where applicable, to enhance period-to-period comparability. The impact of the revision is not material to previously disclosed figures. EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin We define EBITDA as net income plus income tax expense, interest expense, and depreciation and amortization less interest income. We define Adjusted EBITDA as EBITDA with adjustments to exclude results from expenses related to transaction activities, including costs related to planned mergers, acquisitions, and business combinations, non-cash equity-based compensation expense and non-recurring equity restructuring costs. We define Adjusted EBITDA Margin as Adjusted EBITDA divided by revenue. title: How to Build a Business Case for a New HCM System
summary: Learn how to build a business case for a new HCM system by defining needs, estimating ROI, aligning stakeholders, and comparing vendors.
body_text: Choosing a new human capital management (HCM) system is not just an HR technology decision. It is a business decision that can affect the HR team’s productivity and the business’s long-term growth. The strongest HCM proposals do more than compare features. They show leadership why change matters, what the organization can gain, and how the investment supports broader business priorities. A well-built business case helps decision-makers move from “Do we really need a new system?” to “Which solution fits where we are going?” Start with the Problems Your Current System Cannot Solve Before you can justify a new HCM system, clearly define what is not working today. This may include manual payroll workarounds, disconnected HR and benefits data, limited reporting, inconsistent onboarding, duplicate data entry, compliance risk, or limited manager and employee self-service. Be specific. Instead of saying, “Our system is inefficient,” identify the exact points of friction. For example: How many hours does HR spend correcting payroll errors? How long does it take to onboard a new employee? How often do managers request reports that must be built manually? Where does employee data live, and how many systems must be updated when something changes? Connect HCM Needs to Business Goals Executives are more likely to support an HCM investment when the case aligns with priorities they already care about. That may include growth, operational efficiency, risk reduction, employee retention, workforce planning, or better decision-making. For example, if the organization is expanding into new locations, a scalable HCM system can support consistent hiring, onboarding, time tracking, and payroll processes across locations. If leaders are focused on retention, better workforce insights and employee self-service may help improve the employee experience. If compliance is a concern, stronger reporting, audit trails, and centralized data can help reduce risk. Build a Cross-Functional Team Early HCM touches more than HR. Payroll, finance, operations, IT, managers, and employees all rely on accurate workforce data and efficient processes. Bringing these groups into the conversation early helps create a more complete view of current pain points and future requirements. A cross-functional team can also help prevent a common mistake: choosing a platform based only on one department’s needs. The right HCM system should support the full employee lifecycle and align with how the organization operates. Define the Value of Change A strong business case should include both quantitative and qualitative value. Start by estimating the time, cost, and risk associated with the current process. Then identify what could improve with a more unified HCM platform. Time savings: Reduce manual entry, duplicate tasks, and reporting delays. Cost control: Lower administrative burden, reduce system workarounds, and consolidate point solutions when appropriate. Risk reduction: Improve data accuracy, strengthen compliance support, and create more reliable audit trails. Employee experience: Give employees easier access to pay, benefits, schedules, onboarding tasks, and HR information. Decision-making: Give leaders and managers more timely workforce insights. The goal is not to promise unrealistic savings. It is to show a credible path from current-state challenges to measurable business outcomes. Anticipate Stakeholder Questions Before presenting your recommendation, prepare for the questions leaders are likely to ask: What business problems are we solving? Why now? Who will be involved in the evaluation and implementation? What systems need to connect? What risks exist if we delay the decision? How will we measure success after go-live? Answering these questions early strengthens the business case and helps stakeholders view the investment as a structured decision, not a rushed technology request. Once leadership agrees that change is needed, the next step is to evaluate vendors with a clear understanding of your requirements, priorities, and success measures. That is where a structured buying process can help. Get CBIZ’s HCM Buyer’s Guide and Toolkit Use these resources to organize requirements, ask vendors the right questions, and compare solutions with more confidence. Get the Guide FAQ It may be time to replace your HCM system when manual workarounds, duplicate data entry, delayed reporting, or disconnected tools make HR and payroll processes harder to manage. An HCM software decision should involve HR, payroll, finance, IT, operations, and business leaders so the selected platform supports people, process, technology, and budget requirements. An HCM business case should include current challenges, business goals, estimated costs, expected ROI, stakeholder needs, vendor requirements, implementation planning, and success measures. HR can build confidence by involving stakeholders early, using clear data to support the need for change, defining what success will look like after implementation, and comparing vendors against agreed-upon requirements. © Copyright CBIZ, Inc. title: D-Wave Demonstrates Major Hardware Breakthrough for Quantum Error Correction, Advancing the Path to Practical, Fault-Tolerant Gate-Model Quantum Computing
body_text: New peer-reviewed paper published in Nature confirms D-Wave’s gate-model technology can deliver efficient quantum error correction with significantly lower hardware overhead as systems scale Research validates D-Wave's dual-rail technology as a scalable foundation for commercial, fault-tolerant gate-model quantum computing PALO ALTO, Calif. — August 5, 2026 — D-Wave Quantum Inc. (Nasdaq: QBTS), (“D-Wave” or the “Company”), the only dual-platform quantum computing company providing both annealing and gate-model systems, software, and services, today announced a major research breakthrough advancing the path to practical, fault-tolerant gate-model quantum computing. Published in the peer-reviewed scientific journal Nature , the research demonstrates a fast, high-fidelity, two-qubit entangling gate that preserves the error-correction advantages of D-Wave’s superconducting dual-rail qubit architecture. The results address one of the industry’s most consequential challenges by reducing the immense quantum and classical hardware overhead typically required to detect and correct quantum errors as systems scale. The paper, “An entangling gate for dual-rail erasure qubits,” details a new two-qubit entangling gate, a fundamental building block of quantum computation, designed to support efficient quantum error correction. The research demonstrates approximately 99.9% fidelity during two-qubit operations, with fast gate times of about 500 nanoseconds, enabled by native hardware-level error detection. Leveraging these results, D-Wave simulations indicate its dual-rail architecture could reduce the logical error rate by as much as a factor of 10 for each increment in error correction, significantly reducing the physical qubit overhead required for fault-tolerant quantum computing. “Gate-model quantum computing’s greatest remaining challenge is not simply building more qubits. It is building systems that can correct errors efficiently as they scale,” said Dr. Alan Baratz, CEO of D-Wave. “Superconducting quantum computers are known for speed, but achieving the high fidelity needed for scalable, fault-tolerant systems has remained a challenge. This research demonstrates that our dual-rail architecture combines fast superconducting operations with high-fidelity performance while preserving native hardware-level error detection. We believe that this work confirms our path to commercial fault-tolerant quantum computing is practical and achievable.” Removing a Major Barrier to Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Quantum information is inherently fragile and highly susceptible to errors, making efficient quantum error correction essential for the development of reliable, fault-tolerant gate-model quantum computers. In many gate-model architectures, correcting those errors requires large numbers of additional physical qubits and operations, creating substantial engineering complexity, cost, and performance constraints. D-Wave’s dual-rail architecture is designed to create a favorable error hierarchy in which the most common quantum errors are also the easiest to correct. The newly published research demonstrates that this favorable error hierarchy is preserved during two-qubit operations, with the technology maintaining both speed and high fidelity. The results establish an important foundation for scalable quantum error correction with substantially lower hardware overhead. “The entangling gate demonstrated through this research is already integrated into our gate-model systems, where it is delivering comparable performance,” said Dr. Robert Schoelkopf, chief scientist at D-Wave. “We believe these results provide strong evidence that the core architectural principles underpinning our gate-model development roadmap can deliver the speed, fidelity and error-correction efficiency required for practical, fault-tolerant quantum computing.” The research supports D-Wave’s recently announced gate-model development roadmap, which targets a 2032 completion of a 100-logical-qubit system capable of successfully performing more than 1 million operations. The roadmap brings together D-Wave’s superconducting dual-rail architecture and integrated cryogenic control technology to enable more efficient error detection and awareness as systems scale. D-Wave’s roadmap is targeting an error reduction rate, or Lambda, of 10. Lambda is a measure of how rapidly a quantum computer’s errors are reduced as more error-correction capability is added. A Lambda of 10 means the system becomes 10 times more reliable with each increment in error correction, making it possible to achieve low logical error rates required for fault-tolerant quantum computing with far fewer physical qubits. “Building a fault-tolerant quantum computer requires systematically solving a series of difficult scientific and engineering challenges, with each success bringing us closer to a scalable system,” said Dr. Trevor Lanting, chief development officer at D-Wave. “This research demonstrates one of the foundational capabilities of our dual-rail architecture and brings us an important step closer to fault-tolerant gate-model quantum computing.” The research further advances D-Wave’s dual-platform strategy of developing complementary annealing and gate-model quantum computing technologies to address the full range of computationally complex problems. Read the paper, “An entangling gate for dual-rail erasure qubits,” in Nature here . Learn more about D-Wave’s gate-model quantum computing here . About D-Wave Quantum Inc. D-Wave is a leader in the development and delivery of quantum computing systems, software, and services. It is the world’s first commercial supplier of quantum computers, and the first and only to offer dual-platform quantum computing products and services, spanning both annealing and gate-model quantum computing technologies. D-Wave’s mission is to help customers realize the value of quantum today through enterprise-grade systems available on-premises and via its Leap™ quantum cloud service, which offers 99.9% availability and uptime. More than 100 organizations across commercial, government and research sectors trust D-Wave to address complex computational challenges using quantum computing. Learn more about realizing the value of quantum computing today and how D-Wave is shaping the quantum-driven industrial and societal advancements of tomorrow: www.dwavequantum.com . title: Union Pacific’s Big Boy No. 4014 Runs on Its Own Steam
summary: Diesel locomotives assist with braking, switching and showcasing commemorative locomotives
body_text: Whenever Union Pacific's legendary Big Boy No. 4014 rolled through towns this year during its historic coast-to-coast tour , one question almost always followed: "Why are there modern diesel engines traveling behind the world’s largest operating steam locomotive?” It's a fair question: Big Boy is a fully functional 1941-era steam locomotive that provides nearly 100% of all pulling power on tour. In fact, Big Boy has traveled several times without diesels , including between Ogden, Utah, to Green River, Wyoming, during this year’s 14-state tour that attracted millions of spectators. So why do diesels often tag along with Big Boy? The answer is fourfold: Dynamic braking : The Big Boy crew often uses the diesel locomotives’ modern-day dynamic braking system to save wear and tear on the historic locomotive and passenger cars’ brake shoes, which are custom made and pricey to replace. Commemorative Locomotives : When Big Boy goes on tour, it gives Union Pacific a chance to showcase its “commemorative locomotives,” which are painted in bright, custom-colored designs to honor milestones, historical figures and organizations. During the last tour, Big Boy was accompanied by both Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern locomotives that celebrated America’s 250th anniversary, along with No. 1616 that honors President Abraham Lincoln, the founder of Union Pacific. Switching operations : During long journeys, there are times when cars need to be added, removed or repositioned in Big Boy’s train consist. It’s easier and faster to do it with the help of diesels. Range: Unlike days of yore, the infrastructure that once kept steam engines operating across the country, including coal and water towers, no longer exist. The Steam Team accounts for this by refilling the locomotive’s water tender and its two auxiliary water cars every night, but there are times the diesels are used to extend Big Boy’s range. The bottom line is that Big Boy doesn’t need the diesels to run, but they provide modern-day support that helps keep this living piece of railroad history running on the rails, turning heads and inspiring a new generation of railroaders to come.

title: Trident Digital Tech Joint Venture Projects Sikaflow Revenue Run-Rate of Approximately US$65 Million Annualized Exiting 2026
summary: Nearly 285,000 small businesses are projected to be running on Sikaflow by December 2026 — six months after the platform’s launch...
body_text: SINGAPORE, Aug. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Trident Digital Tech Holdings Ltd. (Nasdaq: TDTH) (“Trident” or the “Company”), a digital infrastructure holding company focused on building and operating sovereign-scale technology platforms across emerging markets, today announced that Trident Aliska Digital Tech Ghana Ltd (“TADT”), the Company’s 50/50 joint venture, has completed an internal revenue projection for the Sikaflow platform covering August through December 2026. TADT projects December 2026 revenue of approximately GHS 64.1 million, equivalent to an annualized revenue run-rate of approximately GHS 769 million, or approximately US$65.5 million at the Bank of Ghana mid-rate of GH¢11.74 per US$1.00 published for August 11, 2026. Trident holds a 50% equity interest in TADT. Sikaflow commenced commercial operation on June 23, 2026. Across the full five-month projection period, TADT projects cumulative revenue of approximately GHS 163.6 million, or approximately US$13.9 million, with monthly revenue scaling as MSME onboarding accelerates through the fourth quarter. Projected adoption and revenue TADT projects cumulative onboarding to reach 284,883 actively transacting MSMEs by December 2026, measured against an addressable base of more than 2 million micro, small and medium-sized enterprises in its market. The month-by-month projection is set out below. Month (2026) Projected Active MSMEs Projected TADT Revenue (GHS) August 27,476 6,181,688 September 53,708 12,083,494 October 140,860 31,691,387 November 220,300 49,564,196 December 284,883 64,094,402 Five-month total — 163,615,167 Revenue in the projection is generated across four streams: TADT’s contractual commission on taxes collected and remitted through the platform; TADT’s share of point-of-sale device leasing; TADT’s share of transaction processing fees; and fees generated from adjacent services delivered through Sikaflow, including business registration, annual renewals, insurance distribution and pension administration. The joint venture was announced on April 13, 2026 with a stated combined revenue opportunity of up to approximately US$800 million over five years across its platform mandates. Management believes the Sikaflow projection is consistent with the early-stage trajectory of that opportunity. Basis of projection The projection reflects the following principal assumptions: An average monthly transaction volume of approximately GHS 15,000 per actively transacting MSME, equivalent to approximately GHS 500 per day. An effective tax collection rate of 3% applied to transaction volume processed through the platform. A monthly contribution to TADT from point-of-sale device leasing of GHS 50 per actively transacting MSME. A monthly contribution to TADT from transaction processing fees of GHS 5 per actively transacting MSME. A monthly contribution to TADT from adjacent services of GHS 20 per actively transacting MSME. These assumptions are inherently uncertain and are subject to change. Actual adoption, transaction volumes, fee realization and revenue may differ materially from the amounts projected. Investors should read the cautionary statements set out under “Forward-Looking Statements” below. Market context The MSME sector in TADT’s market accounts for approximately 80% of national employment and represents a substantial share of domestic economic activity. Many of these businesses operate without formal financial records, constraining access to credit, supplier finance and growth capital. The International Finance Corporation has estimated that MSMEs across emerging markets face an annual financing gap of approximately US$5.2 trillion. Sikaflow is designed to convert everyday commercial activity into structured digital financial records, building verifiable transaction histories that can support access to financing, supplier relationships and long-term business growth. The platform integrates digital commerce, inventory management, accounting, customer management, automated tax reporting and financial services functionality, and is accessible through Android, iOS, web, POS terminals and USSD channels with offline-capable operation. “A run-rate approaching US$65 million within six months of launch reflects what we believe this platform architecture can do once it reaches scale,” said Soon Huat Lim, Founder, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Trident Digital Tech Holdings Ltd. “We built Sikaflow to sit at the intersection of commerce, tax administration and financial services, and every transaction that moves through it strengthens the economic record of the business behind it. This is the model we intend to replicate.” “We are onboarding businesses that have operated outside the formal financial system for their entire existence, and we are doing it with local ownership and local partnerships,” said Aleem Kumi, Chief Executive Officer of Trident Aliska Digital Tech Ghana Ltd. “The economics of this platform work because Sikaflow solves a problem our entrepreneurs actually have — recordkeeping, tax compliance and access to finance in one place. The projection reflects the demand we are seeing in the market.” Management believes successful execution may create opportunities to deploy comparable digital infrastructure across additional markets, where business formalization, access to finance, tax digitization and digital commerce adoption present broadly similar challenges. About Sikaflow Sikaflow is an integrated digital commerce, accounting, tax automation and financial management platform built for the micro, small and medium-sized enterprise sector. The platform combines point-of-sale technology, inventory management, accounting functionality, automated tax reporting, business analytics and financial services tools in a single ecosystem accessible through Android, iOS, web, POS terminals and USSD channels. Sikaflow is operated by Trident Aliska Digital Tech Ghana Ltd. For more info go to: https://sikaflow.com About Trident Aliska Digital Tech Ghana Ltd Trident Aliska Digital Tech Ghana Ltd is a 50/50 joint venture between Trident and Aliska, formed to jointly develop and commercialize proprietary digital technology solutions for public- and private-sector clients. Trident leads technology development, platform engineering and technical system management, while Aliska focuses on project research, design, securing government approvals and permits, and project funding. The joint venture is governed by a Board of Directors comprising two directors appointed by each party. For more info go to: https://www.tridentaliska.com About Trident Digital Tech Holdings Ltd. (Nasdaq: TDTH) is a Singapore-headquartered digital infrastructure holding company focused on building and operating sovereign-scale technology platforms across emerging markets. The Company’s strategy centers on entering high-growth economies through trusted digital identity infrastructure and expanding across adjacent government technology, digital commerce, cybersecurity, AI and transaction-driven service verticals. title: 25+ Free appointment reminder text templates
summary: Keep your schedule on track with 25+ SMS appointment reminder text templates and best practices to help reduce no-shows and save time.
body_text: Looking to reduce no-shows and the number of back-and-forth messages from clients who need appointment reminders? One study found that an additional reminder text reduced no-shows by 7% and same-day cancellations by 6%. In this article, we provide appointment reminder text templates you can use to remind customers of their scheduled appointments. We also outline some best practices to follow when sending reminder texts. Plus, we’ll show you how you can send appointment reminders automatically and on a case-by-case basis, depending on your business needs. 6 Appointment reminder text message examples to avoid no-shows If you’re looking for appointment reminder template examples, these six business text templates cover some of the most common types. Your appointment reminder texts may have a different tone and message depending on your industry. However, you can use the reminder templates below as a starting point. 1. General appointment reminder text Hi [customer name], I’m [name] from [business name]. Thanks for booking an appointment with us. Just a reminder that your service is on [day, date, time]. Please click this link to reschedule: [URL]. Reply STOP to unsubscribe. 💡 Check out our appointment confirmation texts guide for industry-specific confirmation examples you can send after a customer books time. 2. Friendly SMS appointment reminder Hi [customer name], [name] from [business name] here. This is a reminder that you have an appointment scheduled with [attendee name] for [day, date, time]. We look forward to seeing you. To opt out of text messages, reply STOP. 3. Request to reschedule appointment message Hi [customer name], I’m [name] from [business name] reaching out to reschedule your appointment per your request. Please respond with a date and time convenient for you. To opt out of receiving texts, reply STOP. 4. Reminder with request for required documents Hi [customer name], I’m [name] from [business name]. I’m reaching out to confirm your appointment for [day, date, time] and let you know that we’ll need the following documents to [action item]: 1. [Document 1] 2. [Document 2] 5. Request to cancel appointment message Hi [customer name], we’ve canceled your appointment per your request. If you’d like to reschedule, please respond with a date and time. Reply STOP to opt out of texts. 6. Reminder with link for video or voice call appointment Hi [customer name], I’m [name] from [business name]. Thank you for booking a 30-minute consultation call with us. Here’s the link for our video chat on [date, time]: [link] Please respond to confirm or reschedule the appointment. 💡If you’re looking to follow up with customers regarding any amount owed, check out our guide to payment reminder messages . 21 SMS appointment reminder templates by industry Need to send an appointment reminder text specific to your industry? We’ve collected 21 of the most common text examples to help you reach customers quickly. If you’re already a Quo, formerly OpenPhone, customer, you can save a text message template on your account. That way, you can quickly send reminders without repetitively typing the same message. 1. Healthcare appointment reminder Hi [customer name]. You’ve scheduled an appointment with Dr. [name] at [business name] for [day, time]. Please respond to this text to confirm or reschedule the appointment. You can also reply STOP to opt out of texts. Note: Healthcare professionals should avoid sharing protected health information over SMS. You must send HIPAA-compliant texts to avoid potential legal issues. 2. Real estate SMS appointment reminder Hi [customer name]. I’m [name] from [business name], and we’re excited to show you [listing address] on [day, time]. Please text this number if you have any questions. Thanks. Check out our real estate text messaging guide for more examples to help you nurture your client relationships . 3. Salon appointment reminder Hi [customer name]. I’m [name] from [salon name]. Thanks for booking [service #1] and [service #2] with us on [day, time]. Please respond CONFIRM to confirm your appointment or CANCEL to cancel it. Feel free to call us if you have any questions. 4. Personal trainer appointment reminder Hi [customer name]. I’m [personal trainer name] from [gym name]. Our training session starts at [time] on [date]. Please confirm the appointment by responding CONFIRM to this message. Respond CANCEL if you’d like to cancel or reschedule the appointment. 5. Tax consultation appointment reminder Hi [customer name]. I’m [consultant name] from [tax consulting company name], reaching out to confirm our appointment scheduled for [time] on [day, date]. Please fill out our intake form and upload documents at [link] so your tax professional can prepare. We’re looking forward to working some magic on your property! 💡 Looking for more ways to reduce no-shows? Check out our guide to stopping last-minute cancellations . How to write an appointment reminder text Effective reminder texts are short and clear, but still include all the necessary details: Personalization. Include the customer’s name and type of appointment , such as fixing a leaking pipe. Clear appointment details. Include the date, time, location, and any parking instructions. Simple confirmation mechanism. Add a call to action like, “Reply Y to confirm or R to reschedule,” or include a reschedule link. Opt-out option. Include an opt-out in every text, like “Reply STOP to unsubscribe.” Business identification. Include your name and your business name in your first message to follow SMS compliance . Here’s an example text that follows these effective text reminder writing tips: Hi Sarah, this is Hot Box Fitness. Reminder: Your boxing class is scheduled for Thursday, Jan 9 at 2:00 p.m. at our downtown location. Reply Y to confirm or R to reschedule. Reply STOP to unsubscribe. When to send appointment reminder texts Here’s a simple schedule that works for most businesses: Immediate confirmation. Within five minutes of booking, send a confirmation that says, “We’ve got you down,” to build trust. Week-before reminder. For appointments scheduled over seven days out, you can send an early reminder. It gives clients a big window to reschedule if needed. 24–48-hour reminder. This is the classic reminder. Send it 24 to 48 hours before the appointment. It’s the perfect window for clients to confirm or reschedule without throwing your whole day into chaos. Day-of nudge. For some businesses — like home services where you need someone to be there — a quick “we’re on our way” text an hour or two before is a nice touch. For others, it might be overkill. You know your clients best. How to send a reminder text from your iPhone If you have an iPhone, there are three apps you can use to send a reminder text: the Shortcuts app, the Reminders app, and the Messages app. Let’s take a closer look at each one. Send a reminder text from your iPhone using the Shortcuts app Shortcuts is a built-in iPhone app that lets you set up simple automations, like sending reminder texts. For texting, it only supports repeating messages on a daily, weekly, or monthly basis. If you only want to send a one-time reminder, you’ll need to delete the automation afterward or use another texting app or service. Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to use the Shortcuts app to send a reminder text: Open the Shortcuts app. Tap on Automation . Select the New Automation button to create a new automation. Select Time of Day . Set the time you want to send the message. Choose how often you want the message to repeat — Daily, Weekly, or Monthly. If you want to double-check the message before it’s sent, ensure the Run After Confirmation setting is on. Tap Next in the top right-hand corner. Choose Send Message . Enter the message you want to send in the Message section. Click on Recipients and add the people you want to receive the message. Select Done . If necessary, delete the automation after the message is sent to avoid sending repeat reminder texts. Before you can start sending reminder texts to US numbers, you’ll need to complete a quick registration called A2P 10DLC. It’s something mobile carriers require to help your messages get delivered reliably. Here’s our 10DLC registration guide for small businesses. Send a reminder text from your iPhone using the Reminders app The Reminders app on your iPhone doesn’t send texts for you. It only gives you a notification at the time you choose, so you’ll still need to open your Messages app and send the text yourself. This can be easy to miss if you’re busy or away from your phone. If you’re looking for a personal reminder to send a message, here’s how to do it: Go to the Reminders app. Tap New Reminder . Write a title , like “Send a reminder text to [name of customer].” Tap Details . Set the date and time you want to receive the reminder. You can also choose When Messaging and choose a contact from your address book. Select Add when you’re finished. Remember, the Reminders app doesn’t automatically send text messages. You’ll still need to send the message yourself. Send a reminder text from your iPhone using the Messages app If your iPhone is running iOS 18 or later, you can schedule texts directly in the Messages app, but only when you’re texting another iMessage user. You can only schedule messages up to 14 days in advance, so it’s not a fit for reminders you want to plan further out. If you need to schedule a quick message in the next two weeks, here’s how to do it with the Messages app: Go to the Messages app and tap the compose message icon on the top right-hand corner. Choose the contact and write your message. Click + on the left of the message box. Tap Send Later . Set the date and time you want the message to be sent. You can choose up to 14 days in advance. Select Send . How to send a reminder text message from your Android device There are a few ways to send event reminder texts and other recurring messages from an Android device. Each option has its strengths and limitations. Let’s explore them. How to send a reminder text using Google Messages Google Messages lets you schedule one-time messages, but it doesn’t support recurring texts. If you need to send the same reminder daily or weekly, you’ll have to schedule each one manually. Here’s how to schedule a one-time message in Google Messages: Open the Messages app on your Android device. Write your message. Press and hold the Send button. Choose a preselected time or pick the date and time you want to send your message. How to send a reminder text on an Android using the Google Calendar app Google Calendar doesn’t have built-in SMS features. You’ll need to connect with a third-party app to send a calendar invite via text . But you can add notifications to Google Calendar events. These notifications will pop up on the recipient’s phone if notifications are turned on. Here’s how to add a notification: Open the Google Calendar app on your Android device. Click the + Create button to create a new event. Choose Event . Add a title, date, time, and who you’re inviting. Leave the default notification at 10 minutes or choose Add notification and select a different time, minutes before, hours, days, or weeks), then tap Done . Select Save . How to send a reminder text using Quo While iPhones, Androids, and calendar apps can help with basic reminder texts, they often fall short for small businesses, especially if you need to schedule one-time messages, send reminders to non-iMessage users, or manage multiple conversations. That’s where a business phone system like Quo comes in. You can easily manage all your call and text conversations while saving time messaging. With Quo, you can schedule one-time or recurring reminder texts that go out automatically — no manual follow-up or extra steps needed. Messages can be sent to any number, and you can even cancel a scheduled message if the person replies before it’s sent. Here’s how to send a reminder text using Quo’s browser or desktop app: Go to the conversation where you want to schedule a reminder text. Draft your message. Click on the Clock icon in the bottom right corner of the message box. Set the date, time zone, and time to send the message. You can also choose to automatically unschedule your message if the recipient messages you first. How to send a reminder text from the Quo iOS or Android app Let’s break down how to send a reminder text from the Quo app: Open Quo on your mobile device. Choose the contact. Enter your message. Tap on the Clock icon in the bottom right-hand corner of the message box. Set the date and time you want to send the message. Under Condition , decide whether you want to automatically cancel your message if the recipient messages you first. Pick the appropriate time zone. How to send a reminder text using Quo’s Zapier and Make integration Integrations allow you to connect multiple apps. Quo’s integrations with Zapier and Make can help you send reminder texts. Here’s a quick look at how you can use them: Note: Zapier and Make aren’t HIPAA compliant, so don’t use them to store, send, or automate anything involving protected health information, or PHI. Zapier You can use integrations with Zapier to create automated appointment text reminders once a customer books a time slot on your Google Calendar, Calendly, or similar appointment scheduling app . Here’s how it works: When a customer books an appointment, Zapier tells Quo to send a personalized reminder text. Just set it up once, and it runs quietly in the background, helping you stay organized and on time. Zapier can also automatically send texts to multiple people at once and more. Make Make gives you even more flexibility with custom workflows. You can connect Google Calendar to Quo and trigger reminder texts when an appointment is approaching. For example, a text can go out a day before the appointment — whatever makes the most sense for your schedule. Need more flexibility? Use the Quo API to build custom workflows that send reminder texts with any tools you already use. 8 best practices for sending appointment reminder texts Be mindful of these best practices when automating SMS appointment reminders: Obtain consent. You need to get permission from a contact before sending them automated event reminders so your messages aren’t flagged as spam. You can get SMS consent in a digital or physical form; just be sure to keep the record on file. Also be sure to include clear opt-out language in each text, such as “If you wish to no longer receive texts from us, reply with STOP.” Get verified with the large US cell carriers. If you’re using a virtual phone service to send business texts to the US, you need to submit your business profile to The Campaign Registry , a third-party organization selected by the major US cell carriers. Quo users can complete this verification step by filling out the US carrier registration form . Keep messages short. Be direct and concise, but not at the expense of important details. You still need to include your name, the appointment time, and other relevant details. Use a phone number people can reply to. Make responding to your text reminders easier by not using a short code. Identify yourself. Identify yourself along with your business name when you send the first message to avoid being marked as spam. Use the same number for communicating with a customer. You should send all texts from your dedicated business number — instead of just appointment reminder software . This makes it easier to catch up on any conversation because all phone communication appears in the same thread. Be on brand. Don’t make automated texts sound robotic. Your text messages should reflect your brand’s voice. Schedule text messages based on the recipient’s time zone. If your client is in Japan and you’re based in New York, it’s best not to schedule a text message for 11 a.m. EST. Instead, determine the recipient’s business hours based on their time zone, convert the time into your local time, and schedule the text to send during those hours. Improve no-show rates with appointment reminder texts in Quo Appointment reminders allow you to optimize your time and avoid the pitfalls of last-minute cancellations. This puts you in a better position to maximize productivity when you know about canceled appointments beforehand. Appointment reminders are a great way to reduce no-show rates. Looking for more ways to prevent no-shows and last-minute cancellations? Check out our guide to cancellation policy templates you can use to communicate your team’s policy to customers or try appointment reminder calls . Frequently asked questions about appointment reminder texts How many appointment reminders should I send? Start with two: an immediate confirmation text right after they book and another 24 hours before the appointment. Some businesses also send a third “we’re on our way” text for house calls, but two is effective for many businesses. What if customers don’t respond to my reminder texts? A non-response doesn’t always mean a no-show. Depending on your cancellation policy, either assume they’re coming or follow up with a quick phone call or text a few hours before. Can I use the same reminder template for all appointment types? You can, but personalization helps. New clients might need your full address or a link to intake forms, while regulars just need a quick confirmation. Adjust your templates to be helpful, not robotic. How do I avoid having my appointment reminders marked as spam? Always get permission to text your clients first, use a dedicated 10-digit business number instead of a short code, and introduce yourself in the first message. Register your number with the US carriers and communicate like a person, not a bot. Is it legal to send reminder texts to customers? Yes, but you need your customer’s permission before sending reminder texts. If you’re texting US phone numbers, you’ll also need to complete US carrier registration before you can send messages. Every reminder text should include a clear way for customers to opt out of future messages, such as “Reply STOP to unsubscribe.” It’s also a good idea to use scheduled texts to send reminders during your recipients’ normal business hours, which helps ensure you stay TCPA compliant . Can I send reminder texts from my business landline? Yes. You can send reminder texts from your business landline by porting it to Quo . Do customers have to opt in to receive reminder texts? Yes. Under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act , or TCPA, businesses must get a customer’s express written consent before sending them text messages. Businesses that don’t follow TCPA rules can face fines issued by the Federal Communications Commission. Keep proof of consent on file, such as the original consent form, the keyword the customer texted to opt in, or the conversation where they agreed to receive messages. Are appointment reminder texts HIPAA compliant? SMS and MMS aren’t HIPAA compliant by default. Healthcare organizations can still use them in a manner consistent with HIPAA regulations if they get appropriate patient authorization, limit protected health information to the minimum necessary, and use a HIPAA-compliant phone system like Quo that supports calling and texting in a compliant manner. Organizations should also document their decision to use SMS or MMS , along with the associated risks, in their HIPAA policies. With Quo, once you have an active account, you can request a BAA in 15 seconds or less on a Business or Scale plan. Why should businesses send reminder texts? Here are three ways reminder texts can help your business: Spend less time reminding customers about appointments. Instead of calling every customer yourself, schedule reminder texts to go out automatically. That frees up your team to focus on other work. Make it easy for customers to confirm, cancel, or reschedule. For some customers, it’s easier to reply to a text than call your business. That means you’re more likely to find out sooner if they need to cancel or reschedule, giving your team more time to update your calendar. Give yourself more time to fill canceled appointments. When a customer lets you know they can’t make it, you have more time to offer that appointment to someone else. Do you need a text reminder service for your business? Not necessarily. Many businesses start by scheduling appointment reminder texts from their personal phones. But once you’re managing more appointments, it’s easy for reminders to slip through the cracks. You can use Quo as a text reminder service with other tools in your tech stack, such as Zapier or Calendly to help you keep up without missing appointments or leaving money on the table.

body_text: The UK’s healthcare system is facing a new seasonal challenge as extreme summer temperatures place increasing pressure on hospitals, emergency departments, and vulnerable communities. Health leaders have warned that heatwaves are becoming a major public health concern and that the NHS must prepare for summer pressures in the same way it has traditionally prepared for winter flu outbreaks. With climate change contributing to longer and more intense periods of hot weather, experts say the country must improve its ability to respond to heat-related illnesses, protect vulnerable people, and reduce preventable deaths during extreme temperatures. The warning comes after thousands of heat-related deaths were recorded during recent heatwaves, highlighting the growing impact of rising temperatures on public health across England. NHS Faces Growing Pressure During Extreme Heat Health Secretary Yvette Cooper has said the NHS needs a stronger approach to managing the risks associated with summer heat. She warned that extreme weather is creating a new type of pressure for hospitals, with emergency departments experiencing demand levels usually associated with winter months. Traditionally, the NHS prepares for seasonal challenges such as influenza outbreaks, respiratory infections, and increased hospital admissions during colder months. However, officials now believe that heatwaves require the same level of planning and preparation. Hospitals across England have reported increased demand during periods of extreme heat, with some facilities facing significant operational pressures. Emergency departments have experienced record levels of attendance, making it increasingly important for healthcare services to develop long-term strategies for managing heat-related health risks. Heatwaves Are Becoming a Serious Public Health Threat Recent figures show the deadly impact of extreme temperatures. According to health officials, thousands of additional deaths have been linked to heatwaves during the summer months. The UK Health Security Agency has highlighted that older adults, people with existing medical conditions, young children, and those who are socially isolated are among the groups most at risk during periods of extreme heat. Heat can affect the body in several ways. Prolonged exposure to high temperatures can lead to dehydration, heat exhaustion, heatstroke, worsening heart conditions, breathing difficulties, and increased risks for people with chronic illnesses. Experts have warned that as the climate continues to warm, the UK can expect heatwaves to become more frequent, longer lasting, and more severe. Why Vulnerable People Need Extra Support Public awareness is considered an important part of reducing heat-related illness and deaths. Health officials are encouraging people to check on elderly relatives, neighbours, and vulnerable individuals during hot weather. Simple actions can make a significant difference. These include ensuring people have access to drinking water, helping them keep their homes cool, encouraging them to avoid direct sunlight during the hottest parts of the day, and checking whether they need medical support. Health leaders have compared this approach to the way communities support vulnerable people during freezing winter weather. Just as people often check on elderly neighbours during cold spells, similar care and attention are needed during extreme summer temperatures. Young children and babies are also vulnerable because they can become affected by heat more quickly than adults. Parents and carers are advised to take precautions to prevent overheating and dehydration. Preparing the NHS for Future Summer Emergencies The NHS is now being urged to develop stronger summer preparedness plans. These could include improved heatwave response systems, better communication with the public, and additional support for hospitals during periods of extreme temperatures. Healthcare planning has historically focused heavily on winter pressures, but changing weather patterns mean summer demand needs greater attention. A more resilient approach could involve: Early warnings for healthcare providers before extreme heat events Public information campaigns about heat safety Additional support for high-risk communities Better monitoring of heat-related hospital admissions Stronger coordination between health organisations and local authorities By preparing earlier, health services may be better able to reduce pressure on emergency departments and prevent avoidable illnesses. Climate Change and the Future of UK Summers The increasing frequency of extreme heat events is closely linked to wider climate changes. Scientists have warned that rising global temperatures are changing weather patterns and increasing the likelihood of severe heatwaves. For the UK, a country historically known for cooler summers, these changes present new challenges. Buildings, transport systems, workplaces, and healthcare services were not always designed for prolonged periods of extreme heat. Adapting to warmer conditions will require action across society. This includes improving public awareness, creating cooler living environments, protecting vulnerable groups, and ensuring essential services can operate effectively during extreme weather. What Individuals Can Do During Heatwaves While government and healthcare organisations play an important role, individuals can also take steps to protect themselves and others. During very hot weather, people should: Drink plenty of fluids regularly Avoid spending long periods in direct sunlight Keep indoor spaces as cool as possible Wear lightweight clothing Check on vulnerable family members and neighbours Seek medical advice if symptoms of heat-related illness appear Warning signs of serious heat-related illness can include confusion, dizziness, severe weakness, difficulty breathing, and loss of consciousness. Anyone experiencing severe symptoms should seek urgent medical assistance. Conclusion Heatwaves are becoming a significant challenge for the UK’s healthcare system. The NHS is being urged to treat summer heat pressures with the same seriousness as winter health emergencies. As temperatures continue to rise, preparing for extreme heat will become an essential part of protecting public health. Better planning, stronger community support, and increased awareness can help reduce the impact of future heatwaves. The message from health experts is clear: extreme heat is no longer a rare summer inconvenience. It is a growing health risk that requires preparation, cooperation, and long-term action.

title: What Is Shift at Midnight? The Viral Skinwalker Gas Station Horror Game, Explained
summary: Shift at Midnight is the viral co-op horror game about spotting skinwalkers on a gas station night shift. Release date, price, platforms, gameplay and how to play free.
body_text: If your feed is full of clips of gas station clerks staring at an ID, hesitating, and then either apologising or opening fire, you have met Shift at Midnight - the co-op horror game that turned a minimum-wage night shift into the most stressful job in gaming. Here is everything you need to know. The pitch: check IDs, spot the thing wearing a face Shift at Midnight is an online cooperative detective horror game. You and up to two others work randomly generated shifts at a rural gas station, and your job is to investigate your customers - because some of them are only pretending to be human. The tells are small and the pressure is constant. You examine an ID, cross-check the details on the store computer, and watch how the person in front of you behaves. Get it wrong and a creature walks into your store, at which point the game stops being paperwork and becomes survival: board the doors, set traps, find somewhere to hide. How the gameplay works Customers arrive one at a time. Serve them, verify them, or turn them away. Every shift is randomly generated, so there is no memorising the answers. Verification means comparing the ID, the computer records, and the person's behaviour for contradictions. Let the wrong one in and the game flips to a chase - barricading, traps, hiding, stamina management. Proximity chat means your teammates' panic is diegetic. It is the best and worst feature in the game. Who made it Shift at Midnight is the work of a single developer, Bun Muen, exclusively licensed to publisher Kwalee. It is the kind of release that keeps proving a small, sharp idea beats a big budget. Release date, price and platforms Shift at Midnight launched on 22 July 2026 on Steam for PC, and arrived on Xbox the same day, including day-one availability on Xbox Game Pass. It sits at roughly $9.99, and there is a free Shift at Midnight Multiplayer Demo on Steam if you want to try before buying. Reception has been strong - Very Positive on Steam, with 94% of thousands of reviews positive. A free Endless Mode update has been announced for later in 2026. Player count and co-op The game is built for 1-3 players online. You can play it solo, and a post-launch update widened lobbies past three, but the developer has stressed the intended experience is a trio. Crossplay is partial: the Xbox console and PC Game Pass versions share a pool, while Steam players match with Steam players. For more on going it alone, read our single-player breakdown . Why it went viral Shift at Midnight sits at the intersection of two proven formats: the identity-verification horror of That's Not My Neighbor, and the proximity-chat co-op chaos of Lethal Company and Phasmophobia. Both are extremely clippable, and TikTok did the rest - double faces, mutations mid-transaction, and clerks shooting the wrong customer have all done numbers. The skinwalker framing gave it a hook that needs no explanation to anyone who has spent five minutes on horror TikTok. How to play something like it for free If you want the fantasy without the purchase, the download, or the two friends, Six Midnight Shifts is a free browser game inspired by it. Six nights on a convenience store graveyard shift: serve impatient customers, maintain the store, check faces and answers against county records, and keep the sidearm holstered until you are certain. Play it free here , or read our full free-to-play guide . It was built with Rosebud AI - if you would rather make your own skinwalker game, here is how to build one without coding . Frequently asked questions When did Shift at Midnight come out? It launched on 22 July 2026 on Steam and Xbox. How much does Shift at Midnight cost? Around $9.99, and it is included with Xbox Game Pass. A free multiplayer demo is available on Steam. How many players is Shift at Midnight? It is designed for 1-3 players online, though a post-launch update allows larger lobbies. Who developed Shift at Midnight? Solo developer Bun Muen, published by Kwalee. Is there a free version? The official game is paid, but there is a free Steam demo, and a free browser game inspired by it called Six Midnight Shifts.
